tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the local-first NL2SQL service, its supported database backends, and its approval-first operating model. It provides the roadmap for the provider, workflow, persistence, safety, and operational areas explored in the remaining steps.

tour.title: Ways to Run
tour.description: The CLI serves scripts and CI, while the Streamlit application provides the interactive multipage experience. Both interfaces converge on the same application layers, so the choice changes the presentation rather than the safety or execution contract.

tour.title: Runtime Configuration
tour.description: Validated settings collect provider, database, persistence, and query-warning options before work begins. This boundary keeps sensitive connection and credential configuration out of the UI and workflow code that consume it.
tour.languageLesson: Typed settings centralize environment parsing and validation so incorrect configuration fails at startup rather than in the middle of a generated-query workflow.

tour.title: Providers and Pricing
tour.description: The model factory selects and constructs chat models across local Ollama and five hosted providers, while the pricing module estimates usage cost. Keeping provider behavior and cost rules together gives the interfaces a consistent catalog for selection, budgeting, and later reporting.

tour.title: Approval-First Workflow
tour.description: The workflow coordinates schema retrieval, SQL generation, validation, preflight planning, approved execution, summarization, usage capture, and auditing. Its typed state makes the generated query and its approval status explicit, preventing an interface action from bypassing the governed path.

tour.title: SQL Policy Gate
tour.description: Before either database backend sees model output, the SQL validator parses, bounds, normalizes, and checks it against policy. This is the central trust boundary: generated SQL is untrusted until it has passed structural checks and produced an approved prepared query.
tour.languageLesson: AST-based validation examines SQL structure instead of relying on keyword filters, which supports allow-lists, single-statement rules, table restrictions, and backend-specific escape-hatch blocking.

tour.title: SQLite and PostgreSQL
tour.description: The backend protocol gives the workflow a shared query-plan and runtime-metrics contract, then concrete SQLite and PostgreSQL adapters enforce backend-specific read-only safeguards. SQLite handles the local demo path, while PostgreSQL verifies role and transaction safety before introspection, planning, or execution.

tour.title: Sessions and Privacy
tour.description: The persistence layer stores local sessions, pending approvals, safe messages, pricing rules, costs, and run metrics while deliberately excluding raw result payloads where appropriate. Privacy-aware audit logging complements it by hashing questions and redacting SQL literals before durable records are written.

tour.title: Costs and Insights
tour.description: The Streamlit page layer turns saved state into actionable views: session resume, cost totals and exports, effective-dated pricing and budget alerts, query-runtime trends, plan warnings, and recent runs. This makes the operational effects of provider choice and approved execution visible after the workflow completes.

tour.title: Evaluation Evidence
tour.description: The evaluation runner executes the JSONL corpus and measures result quality, safety, latency, usage, cost, and database immutability. It provides a repeatable evidence loop for changing prompts, providers, pricing, or backend behavior without relying only on manual UI checks.

tour.title: Safety Test Suite
tour.description: Focused tests cover approval preparation, persistence privacy, PostgreSQL role and plan hardening, provider pricing, and parser-backed SQL policy enforcement. Together they protect the assumptions made in the preceding layers as the application evolves.

tour.title: Delivery and Change
tour.description: The CI workflow synchronizes the locked environment, runs quality and security checks, tests, audits dependencies, and builds the package. Release and migration documentation then explain how the approval, persistence, pricing, PostgreSQL, and insight capabilities change for users over time.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions arrange automated checks into triggered workflows, jobs, and ordered steps; local pre-commit hooks bring selected checks closer to the developer feedback loop.
